research_question: Among women eligible for breast cancer screening, what is the effect of communication-only interventions about mammography screening (decision aids, leaflets, or consultations presenting information on benefits and harms, without an explicit values-clarification exercise), compared with usual information or no intervention, on knowledge about breast cancer screening measured as a continuous score?
treatment_label: Communication/information-only intervention about breast cancer screening (decision aid, leaflet, or consultation with benefit-and-harm information, no values-clarification exercise)
control_label: Usual information, standard leaflet, or no intervention (control)
outcome_description: Continuous knowledge score about breast cancer screening/mammography (e.g. number or percentage of correct answers on a questionnaire covering benefits, harms, overdiagnosis, false positives and screening interval). One overall knowledge score per trial, preferring total score (e.g. conceptual plus numerical knowledge combined) over sub-scales. Extracted as post-intervention mean, SD and number of women analysed per arm, at the first assessment after the intervention (immediately post-intervention up to about one month); later follow-ups not used. SDs derived from CIs, p-values, or SE/SEM when necessary (SD = SE × √n; SD ≈ √n × CI width ÷ 3.92), and cluster-randomised trial sample sizes deflated by the design effect 1 + (average cluster size − 1) × ICC.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g means women receiving the communication-only intervention had better (higher) knowledge about breast cancer screening than women receiving usual information or no intervention — i.e. the effect favours the intervention.
search_queries: breast cancer screening decision aid randomised trial knowledge mammography
mammography screening information leaflet benefits harms randomized controlled trial knowledge score
informed decision making mammography overdiagnosis intervention trial knowledge outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial (including cluster-randomised) in women eligible for or considering breast cancer screening (mammography)

Intervention aimed at improving communication or information about mammography screening benefits and harms (decision aid, leaflet, brochure, video, web tool, or consultation) compared with usual information, standard leaflet, or no intervention
Reports a quantitative knowledge outcome about breast cancer screening that can be expressed or converted to a continuous score (mean and SD, SE, CI, t/F or p-value with group sizes)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between an intervention arm and a usual-information/no-intervention control arm (e.g. single-arm pre-post studies only)
No quantitative knowledge outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no means+SDs, SE/CI, t/F values, or convertible proportions)

Intervention includes an explicit values-clarification exercise (clarifying the woman's values and preferences), or the study is unrelated to breast cancer screening knowledge (e.g. treatment decisions, other cancers, or only non-knowledge outcomes such as uptake, intention, anxiety or decisional conflict)
moderators_to_extract: Intervention format (printed leaflet/brochure vs. video/web/multimedia vs. consultation or counselling)
Inclusion of quantitative/numerical risk information on overdiagnosis and false positives
Timing of first post-intervention assessment (immediate vs. up to one month)
Knowledge instrument type (validated multi-item scale vs. ad hoc questionnaire) and score range
Country/health-system setting and mean participant age or screening-eligibility age band
effect_size_note: Pool as standardised mean difference (Hedges' g) with a random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird/REML) model because knowledge questionnaires differ in scale and length. All scales oriented so higher = more knowledge; reverse sign for any scale oriented the other way. Use post-intervention means, SDs and numbers analysed per arm; document any SD derived from CI, p-value or SE (SD = SE × √n). For cluster-randomised trials, divide arm sample sizes by the design effect 1 + (m̄ − 1) × ICC using the reported ICC or a stated assumed value. For multi-arm trials, combine all communication-only arms into a single group versus the shared control. Heterogeneity assessed with τ², I² and prediction interval; small-study effects via funnel plot and Egger's test when ≥10 trials.
